items.text: Why ___ our customers usually pay at the end of the quarter rather than at the start?

ok.de: Gewohnheit in der Frage: do/does + Grundform. Zu customers (Plural) passt do.
ok.en: A habit in a question takes do/does + base form. The plural customers takes do.

wrong.de: Nach are steht -ing, hier steht aber die Grundform pay.
wrong.en: After are the verb takes -ing, but the sentence has the base form pay.

wrong.de: customers ist Plural, does passt nur zu he, she und it.
wrong.en: customers is plural; does only goes with he, she and it.

wrong.de: have braucht ein Partizip (paid), nicht die Grundform.
wrong.en: have needs a participle (paid), not the base form.

items.text: My brother ___ not drink coffee after lunch because it keeps him awake all night.

ok.de: Verneinung im Present Simple: does not + Grundform; bei he/she/it steht does.
ok.en: Negative in the present simple: does not + base form; he/she/it takes does.

wrong.de: is not drink gibt es nicht; mit not + Grundform braucht es do/does.
wrong.en: is not drink does not exist; not + base form needs do/does.

wrong.de: brother ist Singular: do passt zu I, you, we, they.
wrong.en: brother is singular: do goes with I, you, we, they.

wrong.de: has braucht ein Partizip (drunk), nicht die Grundform.
wrong.en: has needs a participle (drunk), not the base form.

items.text: Please do not come in; the engineers ___ testing the new scanner right now.

ok.de: Was gerade passiert: am/is/are + -ing. Zu we passt are.
ok.en: What is happening now: am/is/are + -ing. We goes with are.

wrong.de: do + running gibt es nicht; vor -ing steht eine Form von be.
wrong.en: do + running does not exist; -ing needs a form of be.

wrong.de: have + running ist keine Zeitform; „gerade jetzt“ braucht am/is/are + -ing.
wrong.en: have + running is not a tense; “right now” needs am/is/are + -ing.

wrong.de: were ist Vergangenheit, „right now“ meint die Gegenwart.
wrong.en: were is past, but “right now” means the present.

items.text: At the moment I ___ not understand why the report shows two different totals for May.

ok.de: understand ist ein Zustandsverb und steht im Present Simple: do not understand, nie am understanding.
ok.en: understand is a state verb and takes the present simple: do not understand, never am understanding.

wrong.de: am not understand ist keine Form; und understand hat kein -ing.
wrong.en: am not understand is not a form, and understand has no -ing form.

wrong.de: will verschiebt es in die Zukunft; „at the moment“ meint jetzt.
wrong.en: will moves it to the future, but “at the moment” means now.

wrong.de: have not understand gibt es nicht; have braucht das Partizip understood.
wrong.en: have not understand does not exist; have needs the participle understood.

items.text: Our director ___ having dinner with the client tonight, so she will not be in the office.

ok.de: have im Sinn von „essen“ ist eine Handlung und steht mit be + -ing: is having dinner.
ok.en: have meaning “to eat” is an action and takes be + -ing: is having dinner.

wrong.de: has having ist falsch; have als Handlung („essen“) braucht be + -ing.
wrong.en: has having is wrong; the action have (“to eat”) takes be + -ing.

wrong.de: does having gibt es nicht; vor -ing steht be.
wrong.en: does having does not exist; -ing needs be.

wrong.de: will having ist keine Form; will braucht die Grundform.
wrong.en: will having is not a form; will needs the base form.

items.text: Look at this e-mail: the vendor ___ always changing the delivery dates again, and it really annoys me.

ok.de: Ärger über ständige Wiederholung: is/are + always + -ing. Zu vendor passt is.
ok.en: Annoyance at constant repetition: is/are + always + -ing. vendor goes with is.

wrong.de: has always changing ist falsch; für den Ärger braucht es is + always + -ing.
wrong.en: has always changing is wrong; the annoyance needs is + always + -ing.

wrong.de: does always changing gibt es nicht; vor -ing steht be.
wrong.en: does always changing does not exist; -ing needs be.

wrong.de: vendor ist Singular, also is und nicht are.
wrong.en: vendor is singular, so is and not are.

items.text: When ___ the client finally sign the contract, and who was in the room at that point?

ok.de: Frage nach einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit: When did + Subjekt + Grundform.
ok.en: A question about a past point in time: When did + subject + base form.

wrong.de: has braucht ein Partizip (signed); hier steht die Grundform sign.
wrong.en: has needs a participle (signed); the sentence has the base form sign.

wrong.de: was sign ist falsch; in der Frage nach einem Zeitpunkt steht did + Grundform.
wrong.en: was sign is wrong; a question about a point in time takes did + base form.

wrong.de: does ist Gegenwart, die Frage geht aber um etwas Vergangenes.
wrong.en: does is present, but the question is about the past.

items.text: We moved to Frankfurt ___ 2019, and my daughter was born there two years later.

ok.de: Abgeschlossene Zeit mit Jahreszahl: Past Simple und in 2019.
ok.en: A finished time with a year: past simple and in 2019.

wrong.de: since nennt den Anfang bis heute; die Handlung ist aber abgeschlossen.
wrong.en: since names a start up to now, but the action is finished.

wrong.de: for nennt eine Dauer, hier steht aber ein Jahr als Zeitpunkt.
wrong.en: for names a length of time, but here a year is a point in time.

wrong.de: at steht bei Uhrzeiten, nicht bei Jahreszahlen.
wrong.en: at goes with clock times, not with years.

items.text: Our family has used the same holiday cottage ___ 2018, and nobody wants to change it.

ok.de: Dauer bis heute ab einem Zeitpunkt: has/have + Partizip + since + Zeitpunkt.
ok.en: Duration up to now from a point in time: has/have + participle + since + point in time.

wrong.de: for braucht eine Länge („for six years“), keine Jahreszahl.
wrong.en: for needs a length of time (“for six years”), not a year.

wrong.de: in 2018 passt zum Past Simple, nicht zu has used.
wrong.en: in 2018 goes with the past simple, not with has used.

wrong.de: from 2018 braucht ein „to“ oder „until“; mit has used gilt since.
wrong.en: from 2018 needs “to” or “until”; with has used you need since.

items.text: Our firm has supplied the regional hospital ___ more than twenty years, and we have never missed a delivery.

ok.de: Länge der Zeit: for + fifteen years; since stünde nur vor einem Startpunkt.
ok.en: A length of time: for + fifteen years; since only comes before a starting point.

wrong.de: since braucht einen Zeitpunkt („since 2011“), keine Länge.
wrong.en: since needs a point in time (“since 2011”), not a length.

wrong.de: during nennt einen Zeitraum, in dem etwas geschieht, nicht die Länge bis heute.
wrong.en: during names a period in which something happens, not the length up to now.

wrong.de: in passt nicht zu einer Länge von Jahren mit have known.
wrong.en: in does not fit a length of years with have known.

items.text: Have you ___ worked with a customer who changed the scope after the contract was signed?

ok.de: Erfahrung im bisherigen Leben fragt man mit Have you ever + Partizip?
ok.en: You ask about experience so far in life with Have you ever + participle?

wrong.de: yet steht am Satzende in Fragen nach einem erwarteten Ereignis.
wrong.en: yet comes at the end of questions about an expected event.

wrong.de: just bedeutet „gerade eben“, nicht „je im Leben“.
wrong.en: just means “a moment ago”, not “at any time in your life”.

wrong.de: soon bedeutet „bald“ und passt nicht zu have worked.
wrong.en: soon means “shortly” and does not fit have worked.

items.text: I have ___ been to Japan, so I have no idea what to expect from the trip next month.

ok.de: Keine Erfahrung bis jetzt: have never been (oder have not been).
ok.en: No experience so far: have never been (or have not been).

wrong.de: ever steht in Fragen oder nach Superlativen, nicht in einer solchen Aussage.
wrong.en: ever belongs in questions or after superlatives, not in a statement like this.

wrong.de: yet passt nicht zwischen have und been in dieser Aussage.
wrong.en: yet does not fit between have and been in this statement.

wrong.de: just bedeutet „gerade eben“ und widerspricht „no idea“.
wrong.en: just means “a moment ago” and contradicts “no idea”.

items.text: Could you check the figures again? The finance team has ___ sent me a corrected version.

ok.de: Gerade eben oder schon passiert, Ergebnis jetzt: has/have + just/already + Partizip.
ok.en: Happened a moment ago or by now, result now: has/have + just/already + participle.

wrong.de: ever steht in Fragen und Verneinungen, nicht in einer solchen Aussage.
wrong.en: ever belongs in questions and negatives, not in a statement like this.

wrong.de: yet steht am Ende von Fragen und Verneinungen, nicht vor dem Partizip.
wrong.en: yet comes at the end of questions and negatives, not before the participle.

wrong.de: ago steht nach einer Zeitangabe und braucht das Past Simple.
wrong.en: ago follows a time expression and needs the past simple.

items.text: I have not decided ___ whether I will accept the new offer, so please give me until Friday.

ok.de: Noch nicht, aber erwartet: have not + Partizip + yet.
ok.en: Not yet, but expected: have not + participle + yet.

wrong.de: already steht in Aussagen, nicht in einer Verneinung wie „have not decided“.
wrong.en: already belongs in statements, not in a negative like “have not decided”.

wrong.de: ever passt nicht zu „have not decided … whether“.
wrong.en: ever does not fit “have not decided … whether”.

wrong.de: still würde vor have not stehen: „I still have not decided“.
wrong.en: still would stand before have not: “I still have not decided”.

items.text: Our two developers ___ been fixing the login bug since Monday morning, and it is still not solved.

ok.de: Dauer bis jetzt mit Handlung: have/has been + -ing; zu two developers (Plural) passt have.
ok.en: Duration up to now with an activity: have/has been + -ing; the plural two developers goes with have.

wrong.de: are been gibt es nicht; vor been steht have/has.
wrong.en: are been does not exist; been needs have/has.

wrong.de: had been bezieht sich auf einen früheren Zeitpunkt; „since Monday … still“ reicht bis jetzt.
wrong.en: had been refers to an earlier point; “since Monday … still” reaches up to now.

wrong.de: were been ist falsch; die Form heißt have/has been + -ing.
wrong.en: were been is wrong; the form is have/has been + -ing.

items.text: The construction crew has been drilling next door ___ four hours, and I cannot make a single phone call.

ok.de: for + Länge der Zeit (four hours), since + Zeitpunkt (since noon).
ok.en: for + length of time (four hours), since + point in time (since noon).

wrong.de: since braucht einen Startpunkt („since noon“), hier steht eine Länge.
wrong.en: since needs a starting point (“since noon”), but here is a length.

wrong.de: during passt nicht zu has been playing + Länge der Zeit.
wrong.en: during does not fit has been playing + a length of time.

wrong.de: from passt nicht ohne „to“; die Länge nennt for.
wrong.en: from does not work without “to”; for names the length.

items.text: Over the ___ few months, orders from the Nordic region have been going up, and the board is finally starting to take notice.

ok.de: Entwicklung in letzter Zeit: over the last/past few months + have been + -ing.
ok.en: A recent development: over the last/past few months + have been + -ing.

wrong.de: next verlangt die Zukunft; have been going up beschreibt die Zeit bis jetzt.
wrong.en: next needs the future; have been going up describes the time up to now.

wrong.de: following passt zu einem Zeitraum nach einem genannten Ereignis.
wrong.en: following fits a period after a named event.

wrong.de: every few months heißt „alle paar Monate“ und beschreibt keine Entwicklung bis jetzt.
wrong.en: every few months means “once in a while” and describes no development up to now.

items.text: How long ___ the delivery truck been standing outside, and has anybody asked the driver what he wants?

ok.de: Frage nach der Dauer bis jetzt: How long + has/have + Subjekt + been + -ing. Zu truck gehört has.
ok.en: A question about duration up to now: How long + has/have + subject + been + -ing. truck takes has.

wrong.de: have passt zu I, you, we, they; ein einzelner Lastwagen verlangt has.
wrong.en: have goes with I, you, we, they; a single truck needs has.

wrong.de: is been ist keine Form; vor been steht has/have.
wrong.en: is been is not a form; been needs has/have.

wrong.de: did + been gibt es nicht; die Dauer bis jetzt braucht has been + -ing.
wrong.en: did + been does not exist; duration up to now needs has been + -ing.

items.text: So ___, we have signed twelve new customers this quarter, but I have been talking to many more.

ok.de: So far = bis jetzt, mit der Zahl als Ergebnis: have signed twelve.
ok.en: So far = up to now, with the number as the result: have signed twelve.

wrong.de: So long heißt „bis bald“ und passt nicht zu einer Zahl.
wrong.en: So long means “goodbye” and does not fit a count.

wrong.de: So much passt hier nicht; „so far“ ist die feste Wendung.
wrong.en: So much does not fit here; “so far” is the fixed phrase.

wrong.de: So well bedeutet „so gut“ und nennt keinen Zeitraum bis jetzt.
wrong.en: So well means “so successfully” and does not name a period up to now.

items.text: Thanks for the reminder about the missing signature; I ___ get it signed by the end of the day, I promise.

ok.de: Entschluss und Versprechen im Gespräch: I will + Grundform.
ok.en: A decision and promise during the conversation: I will + base form.

wrong.de: am get ergibt keinen Satz; für ein Versprechen steht will + Grundform.
wrong.en: am get does not make a sentence; a promise takes will + base form.

wrong.de: do get sagt nichts über die Zukunft.
wrong.en: do get says nothing about the future.

wrong.de: have get gibt es nicht; have braucht got oder gotten.
wrong.en: have get does not exist; have needs got or gotten.

items.text: We ___ going to renovate the kitchen next spring because the old one is falling apart.

ok.de: Ein schon geplantes Vorhaben: am/is/are + going to + Grundform; zu we gehört are.
ok.en: A plan already made: am/is/are + going to + base form; we goes with are.

wrong.de: will + going to kann man nicht verbinden.
wrong.en: will and going to cannot be combined.

wrong.de: do + going to gibt es nicht; vor going to steht am/is/are.
wrong.en: do + going to does not exist; going to needs am/is/are.

wrong.de: have + going to ist falsch; die Form lautet be going to.
wrong.en: have + going to is wrong; the form is be going to.

items.text: I ___ going to send you the minutes yesterday, but my laptop broke and I lost all my notes.

ok.de: Plan, der nicht klappte: was/were going to + Grundform; zu I gehört was.
ok.en: A plan that fell through: was/were going to + base form; I goes with was.

wrong.de: am going to meint die Gegenwart; „my laptop broke“ zeigt, dass der Plan Vergangenheit ist.
wrong.en: am going to is present; “my laptop broke” shows the plan is past.

wrong.de: were passt zu you, we, they; I verlangt was.
wrong.en: were goes with you, we, they; I needs was.

wrong.de: will ist Zukunft; hier geht es um einen geplatzten Plan in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: will is future; this is about a plan that fell through in the past.

items.text: Our train to the lake in Bavaria leaves ___ 7:45 tomorrow morning, so please be at the station by 7:15.

ok.de: Fahrplan im Present Simple, Uhrzeit mit at: leaves at 7:45.
ok.en: A timetable takes the present simple, clock time takes at: leaves at 7:45.

wrong.de: in steht bei Zeiträumen („in May“), nicht bei einer Uhrzeit.
wrong.en: in goes with periods (“in May”), not with a clock time.

wrong.de: on steht bei Tagen und Daten („on Monday“).
wrong.en: on goes with days and dates (“on Monday”).

wrong.de: by heißt „spätestens um“, der Zug fährt aber genau um 7:45.
wrong.en: by means “no later than”, but the train leaves exactly at 7:45.

items.text: Hurry up, the doors of the train are about ___ close, and the next one leaves in an hour.

ok.de: Gleich passiert es: be about to + Grundform.
ok.en: It happens any moment now: be about to + base form.

wrong.de: about for close ist keine Wendung; es heißt be about to + Grundform.
wrong.en: about for close is not a phrase; it is be about to + base form.

wrong.de: about of close gibt es nicht; nach about folgt hier to.
wrong.en: about of close does not exist; to follows about here.

wrong.de: about by close gibt es nicht; die feste Wendung ist about to.
wrong.en: about by close does not exist; the fixed phrase is about to.

items.text: We will not be able to deliver the update on Friday ___ the client sends us the missing data today.

ok.de: unless = außer wenn, mit Gegenwart statt will: unless the client sends.
ok.en: unless = except if, with the present instead of will: unless the client sends.

wrong.de: if ergäbe die falsche Bedeutung: Wir liefern nicht, falls er sendet.
wrong.en: if would give the wrong meaning: we do not deliver if he sends it.

wrong.de: since heißt „weil“ oder „seit“; hier geht es um eine Voraussetzung.
wrong.en: since means “because” or “from the time”; this is a requirement.

wrong.de: although heißt „obwohl“; es gibt keinen Gegensatz, sondern eine Voraussetzung.
wrong.en: although means “even though”; there is no contrast, only a requirement.

items.text: We will start the rollout as ___ as the client has signed off the test report.

ok.de: Zeitsatz mit as soon as und Gegenwart statt will: as soon as the client has signed off.
ok.en: A time clause with as soon as and the present instead of will: as soon as the client has signed off.

wrong.de: as long as bedeutet „solange“ und passt nicht zu „sobald es abgenommen ist“.
wrong.en: as long as means “provided that” and does not fit “as soon as it is signed off”.

wrong.de: as well as heißt „sowie“ und hat keinen Zeitbezug.
wrong.en: as well as means “and also” and has no time reference.

wrong.de: as much as nennt eine Menge, keinen Zeitpunkt.
wrong.en: as much as names an amount, not a point in time.

items.text: When my parents arrive on Saturday, we ___ going to take them to the old town for dinner.

ok.de: Nach when steht die Gegenwart (arrive), nicht will; der Plan selbst: are going to.
ok.en: After when the present is used (arrive), not will; the plan itself: are going to.

wrong.de: will + going to kann man nicht verbinden.
wrong.en: will and going to cannot be combined.

wrong.de: do + going to gibt es nicht; vor going to steht am/is/are.
wrong.en: do + going to does not exist; going to needs am/is/are.

wrong.de: have + going to ist falsch; die Form lautet be going to.
wrong.en: have + going to is wrong; the form is be going to.

items.text: Once the supplier ___ confirmed the delivery slot, we will inform all regional offices.

ok.de: Eine Handlung muss vorher abgeschlossen sein: once + Present Perfect, im Hauptsatz will.
ok.en: An action must be completed first: once + present perfect, will in the main clause.

wrong.de: Nach once steht keine Zukunft mit will.
wrong.en: After once you do not use will.

wrong.de: are confirmed passt nicht zu supplier (Singular) und ist keine Perfektform.
wrong.en: are confirmed does not fit supplier (singular) and is not a perfect form.

wrong.de: had confirmed ist Vergangenheit; hier wird eine künftige Voraussetzung beschrieben.
wrong.en: had confirmed is past; this describes a future condition.

items.text: ___ the time the new CEO starts in January, we will already have moved the whole team into the new building.

ok.de: By the time + Gegenwart: spätestens bis dahin; im Hauptsatz Future Perfect.
ok.en: By the time + present: no later than then; the main clause takes the future perfect.

wrong.de: at the time heißt „damals“ und passt nicht zu einer künftigen Frist.
wrong.en: at the time means “back then” and does not fit a future deadline.

wrong.de: on the time ist keine Wendung.
wrong.en: on the time is not a phrase.

wrong.de: in the time bedeutet „in der Zeit“ und passt nicht zu einer Frist.
wrong.en: in the time means “within the time” and does not fit a deadline.

items.text: I do not know ___ the new software will be ready, but I will ask our IT department tomorrow.

ok.de: In einer indirekten Frage bleibt will (when/if/whether it will be ready); die Gegenwart gilt nur im Zeitsatz.
ok.en: In an indirect question will stays (when/if/whether it will be ready); the present is only for time clauses.

wrong.de: unless heißt „außer wenn“ und leitet keine indirekte Frage ein.
wrong.en: unless means “except if” and does not introduce an indirect question.

wrong.de: until nennt einen Endpunkt und leitet hier keine indirekte Frage ein.
wrong.en: until names an end point and does not introduce an indirect question here.

wrong.de: while heißt „während“ und leitet hier keine indirekte Frage ein.
wrong.en: while means “during the time that” and does not introduce an indirect question here.

items.text: I am not sure ___ my flight will be on time, because there is a strike at the airport.

ok.de: Ja/Nein-Frage nach not sure: whether oder if, und will bleibt.
ok.en: A yes/no question after not sure: whether or if, and will stays.

wrong.de: when fragt nach einem Zeitpunkt; hier geht es um ja oder nein.
wrong.en: when asks for a point in time; this is a yes/no question.

wrong.de: unless heißt „außer wenn“ und leitet keine Frage ein.
wrong.en: unless means “except if” and does not introduce a question.

wrong.de: about braucht ein Nomen oder -ing, keinen ganzen Satz.
wrong.en: about needs a noun or -ing, not a full clause.

items.text: Our support team will keep answering calls ___ the last customer on the line has been helped.

ok.de: until = bis; danach steht die Gegenwart (has been helped), kein will.
ok.en: until = up to the time that; the present follows (has been helped), never will.

wrong.de: unless heißt „außer wenn“; hier ist „bis“ gemeint.
wrong.en: unless means “except if”; here “up to the time that” is meant.

wrong.de: since nennt einen Startpunkt, hier geht es um ein Ende.
wrong.en: since names a starting point, but this is about an end.

wrong.de: while heißt „während“ und passt nicht zu einer abgeschlossenen Handlung (has been helped).
wrong.en: while means “during” and does not fit a completed action (has been helped).
